passage: Arnab was cycling home from tuition when a friend told him, half laughing, that Kalyan liked the boy from the sweetshop family. Arnab kept pedalling, but his chest felt heavy, like a bag of wet sand. At home he ate little and went up to the roof. He cried for a while where nobody could see. Then he told his older cousin, who did not say much, only listened and brought him a glass of water. The next day Kalyan smiled at him at the school tap, as he always did. He smiled back a little late. He wanted to say something mean about the sweetshop boy, but he decided not to.

qa.a: He cried on the roof where nobody could see.

qa.q: What was Arnab feeling when he heard about Kalyan's crush, and how can you tell?
qa.a: He felt hurt and sad, since his chest felt heavy like a bag of wet sand, he ate little and he cried.

qa.q: What helped Arnab cope, and what did he choose not to do?
qa.a: He cried, talked to his cousin who listened, and stayed friendly with Kalyan; he chose not to say something mean about the other boy.

qa.q: How might Kalyan see Arnab's smile at the tap?
qa.a: Kalyan probably has no idea what he is going through, since he smiled as always, and Arnab's late smile may just seem shy to him.

grounding: A child finds out his crush likes someone else, feels the ache, talks to someone and stays kind.

passage:
"Mum, can I talk to you?"
"Of course, Amandeep. What's wrong?"
"You know Nilesh from my class? I found out today he likes Pooja."
"Oh, sweetheart."
"My chest feels all heavy. Like there's a stone in it."
"That feeling is real. It hurts when someone we like likes someone else."
"Some girls said I should say something mean about Pooja."
"What do you think?"
"That it wouldn't help. Pooja's nice. And Nilesh is still my friend."
"That's very grown-up. You can be sad, and you can cry. It won't last forever."
Amandeep leaned against her. "Can we make hot chocolate?"

qa.q: How does Amandeep feel after finding out?
qa.a: Heavy and hurt, as if there's a stone in the chest.

qa.q: What did Amandeep decide about the mean comment idea?
qa.a: That mocking Pooja wouldn't help, because Pooja is nice and Nilesh is still a friend.

qa.q: How might Mum feel listening to Amandeep?
qa.a: Mum seems caring and proud, reassuring that it's okay to be sad and it won't last forever.

grounding: A child learns their crush likes someone else and feels heavy; they talk to a parent, allow the sadness, and choose not to mock the other girl.

passage:
I'm Rehana. In Class 6, I found out Chaitanya liked Farzana. A friend told me at recess, laughing like it was nothing.
My chest felt so heavy I could barely eat my lunch. At home I cried into my pillow.
Then I told Ammi. She held me and said, "This ache is real. It will pass, but you can be sad now."
Some of my friends wanted to make fun of Farzana's teeth. I said no. It wasn't her fault. And Chaitanya had always been kind to me.
It took a few weeks, but it did fade. Chaitanya and I still sit together in computer class.

qa.q: How did Rehana feel on hearing the news?
qa.a: Rehana felt heartbroken and heavy, barely eating and crying into the pillow at home.

qa.q: What helped Rehana cope with the ache?
qa.a: Crying, talking to Ammi, refusing to mock Farzana, and staying friends with Chaitanya.

qa.q: How might Farzana have felt if the friends had made fun of her?
qa.a: Farzana would have been hurt for something that wasn't her fault.

grounding: A child finds out their crush likes someone else; the ache is real but passes, and talking, crying and refusing to mock anyone helps.
